prompt.context: You are working for a bank that is facing problems with the quality of customer service. Its customers are complaining about long waits on the phone, being transferred to multiple branches, separate accounts requiring multiple calls, etc. The customer service function is currently performed at each individual branch.
prompt.question: How can customer service be improved?

framework: Value Chain Analysis: map the current customer service process from the moment a customer calls to resolution — identify each step, handoff, and failure point
Diagnosis of current operations: understand how each call is handled, what customers complain about specifically, and why problems occur
Internal benchmarking: compare performance across branches within the bank to identify best practices and outliers
Competitive benchmarking: analyze how competing banks handle customer service (centralized vs. branch-level, staffing, technology)
Cross-industry benchmarking: look at industries with best-in-class customer service operations (e.g., telecom, insurance, retail) for transferable practices
Recommendation: propose structural or process changes based on findings (e.g., centralization, unified CRM, call routing improvements)

questions.prompt: Diagnose the root causes of the current customer service problems.
questions.guidance: Candidate should explore the operational model: calls are handled at the branch level with no centralization, leading to siloed information. Root causes include: no single view of the customer across accounts, inconsistent training across branches, no intelligent call routing, and lack of shared knowledge bases. The candidate should distinguish between people, process, and technology failure modes.

questions.prompt: How would you benchmark customer service performance, and against whom?
questions.guidance: Three layers of benchmarking: (1) Internal — compare branch-by-branch metrics (average handle time, transfer rate, first-call resolution, customer satisfaction scores) to find which branches perform best and why. (2) Competitive — assess how rival banks structure their customer service (branch-based vs. centralized call centers). (3) Cross-industry — look at sectors like telecom or insurance that operate large-scale customer service centers; identify technology and process best practices transferable to banking.

questions.prompt: What structural changes would you recommend to improve customer service?
questions.guidance: Strong answers should cover: (1) Centralizing customer service into a dedicated call center to eliminate branch-level fragmentation; (2) Implementing a unified CRM so any agent can see all of a customer's accounts; (3) Intelligent call routing (IVR / skills-based routing) to reduce transfers; (4) Standardized training and quality monitoring; (5) Potential for tiered service (simple queries via self-service or chatbot; complex queries to specialized agents). Candidate should weigh cost of centralization against service improvement.

recommendation: Centralize the customer service function into one or more dedicated contact centers, replacing the current branch-by-branch model, to create a single point of contact with a unified customer view
Invest in a shared CRM system so any agent can instantly access all accounts for a calling customer, eliminating the need for multiple transfers or repeat calls
Implement intelligent call routing and tiered service to match customer needs to the right agent on the first try
risks: Change management: branch staff currently handling calls will need retraining or redeployment; union or morale issues possible
Implementation cost of new CRM and telephony infrastructure may be significant
Centralized agents may lack specialized local or product knowledge in the short term
next_steps: Conduct detailed process mapping and call-volume analysis across all branches to size the opportunity
Run a pilot centralized call center for one region and measure first-call resolution, handle time, and customer satisfaction vs. branch baseline
Develop business case comparing cost of centralization against projected revenue retention and NPS improvement
